newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US to work to halt further yen weakening - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US to work to halt further yen weakening - MOF.

text.p: Japan and the United States will put effort into coping with any further weakening of the yen, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee on Thursday.
Mitsuzuka said the message on currencies from last Sunday's Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Washington was stronger than the one issued at the G7 meeting in Berlin in February.
He said Japan and the United States had agreed to keep close cooperative ties on currency stability.
"There is no doubt that we will put effort into coping with further yen weakeness," he said.
Japan also told the United States that now was not the time for Japan to consider additional fiscal measures for its economic recovery.
Although Japan's economy had slowed down somewhat due to the increase in the consumption tax on April 1, the economy was steadily becoming firmer, centring on domestic demand, he said.
He added that he had told the United States that Japan had no intention of depending on external demand, which in theory should grow amid the yen's weakness, to help its economic recovery.
